Start with a module contract

These are integration recipes for your own host application, not prebuilt connectors to a specific CRM, ticket vendor or payment provider. Each names the module inputs, outputs and events you need to create in Lowcoder first. Replace the placeholder application IDs and host actions.

Load bundle.js once as shown in the quickstart, then use these examples inside an async function or JavaScript module. They use the hosted browser SDK. Remove each embed through await sdk.unmount(element) when its screen closes.

Named module events contain only their name. Use outputs for data; an output update and a separate event are not an atomic message. For business mutations, prefer a single structured output with a request ID and deduplicate it in the host/backend.

CRM: a customer workspace

Keep customer navigation and account selection in your CRM. Embed a visually maintained account panel that receives the selected customer and can ask the host to open their record.

Module contract Create in Lowcoder
Inputs customerId (String), customerName (String)
Outputs healthScore (Number) for the host’s summary
Event openCustomer triggered by a module button
JavaScript
const sdk = await LowcoderSDK.ready;
let selected = { id: "customer-42", name: "Morgan Lee" };
const app = await sdk.mount("#crm-panel", {
  appId: "YOUR_CRM_MODULE_ID",
  moduleInputs: { customerId: selected.id, customerName: selected.name }
});
app.on("moduleOutputChange", ({ healthScore }) => {
  document.querySelector("#health-score").textContent = healthScore ?? "—";
});
app.on("moduleEventTriggered", (name) => {
  if (name === "openCustomer") {
    // Use the authoritative selection already held by the host.
    location.assign("/customers/" + encodeURIComponent(selected.id));
  }
});
function selectCustomer(customer) {
  selected = customer;
  app.setModuleInputs({ customerId: customer.id, customerName: customer.name });
}

Create #crm-panel and #health-score in your host. Wire its customer picker to selectCustomer. The health output may arrive later than mount, so the host should display a placeholder until it receives a value.

Website: an interactive product configurator

Place a configuration module inside a product page. The site owns the product route; Lowcoder owns the form, calculations and visual editing. A named event can direct the host to its contact section.

Module contract Create in Lowcoder
Inputs productId (String), options (Array)
Outputs estimatedTotal (Number), calculated by the module
Event requestContact triggered by the visitor
JavaScript
const sdk = await LowcoderSDK.ready;
const app = await sdk.mount("#configurator", {
  appId: "YOUR_CONFIGURATOR_MODULE_ID",
  moduleInputs: {
    productId: "desk-01",
    options: JSON.stringify([
      { id: "oak", label: "Oak", price: 120 },
      { id: "walnut", label: "Walnut", price: 160 }
    ])
  }
});
app.on("moduleOutputChange", ({ estimatedTotal }) => {
  document.querySelector("#estimate").textContent =
    typeof estimatedTotal === "number"
      ? new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { style: "currency", currency: "EUR" })
          .format(estimatedTotal)
      : "Choose your options";
});
app.on("moduleEventTriggered", (name) => {
  if (name === "requestContact") {
    document.querySelector("#contact").scrollIntoView();
  }
});

Create the #configurator, #estimate and #contact elements. Publish the module for the intended audience. Treat the displayed estimate as client-side information; calculate an authoritative price on your backend before accepting an order.

Ticket system: context and escalation

Embed a triage panel alongside a ticket. Send the ticket context as a Data input. Return an escalation request as one structured output, so its ticket ID, reason and request ID travel together.

Module contract Create in Lowcoder
Input ticket (Data): { id, subject, priority }
Output escalationRequest (Data): null, or { requestId, ticketId, reason }
Module action On explicit user escalation, assign a fresh request ID and set the complete output object
JavaScript
const sdk = await LowcoderSDK.ready;
const ticket = { id: "T-1042", subject: "Export failed", priority: "normal" };
const app = await sdk.mount("#ticket-tools", {
  appId: "YOUR_TRIAGE_MODULE_ID",
  moduleInputs: { ticket: JSON.stringify(ticket) }
});
const handled = new Set();
app.on("moduleOutputChange", ({ escalationRequest: request }) => {
  if (!request || typeof request.requestId !== "string" || !request.requestId ||
      request.ticketId !== ticket.id || typeof request.reason !== "string" ||
      handled.has(request.requestId)) return;
  handled.add(request.requestId);
  // Show a host-owned confirmation using safe text rendering.
  // Its submit action calls your ticket API, which validates access
  // and deduplicates requestId. This output is a request, not authorization.
  document.querySelector("#escalation-reason").textContent = request.reason;
  document.querySelector("#escalation-confirmation").hidden = false;
});

Create #ticket-tools and a host confirmation panel containing #escalation-reason. Initialize the module’s request output to null and change it only on a deliberate user action. Keep backend deduplication across remounts; the in-memory set only covers this screen’s lifetime.

POS: a loyalty panel beside the cart

Keep the cart, tender and payment flow in your POS. Embed a loyalty or service panel that receives the current cart and requests an optional lookup or host action.

Module contract Create in Lowcoder
Inputs cart (Array), customerId (String)
Event requestCustomerLookup
Method refreshOffers, with a single customerId parameter
Output offerStatus (String): module-owned loading/success/failure information
JavaScript
const sdk = await LowcoderSDK.ready;
const app = await sdk.mount("#loyalty-panel", {
  appId: "YOUR_LOYALTY_MODULE_ID",
  moduleInputs: {
    customerId: "customer-42",
    cart: JSON.stringify([{ sku: "coffee-01", quantity: 2 }])
  }
});
app.on("moduleEventTriggered", (name) => {
  if (name === "requestCustomerLookup") {
    document.querySelector("#customer-lookup").showModal();
  }
});
app.on("moduleOutputChange", ({ offerStatus }) => {
  document.querySelector("#offer-status").textContent = offerStatus ?? "";
});
// Enable this host control only once the module is visibly usable.
const refreshOffers = () => app.invokeMethod("refreshOffers", ["customer-42"]);
document.querySelector("#refresh-offers").addEventListener("click", refreshOffers);

// When leaving the POS screen, remove host-owned listeners too:
async function closeLoyaltyPanel() {
  document.querySelector("#refresh-offers").removeEventListener("click", refreshOffers);
  await sdk.unmount("#loyalty-panel");
}

Create the panel, a <dialog id="customer-lookup">, status text and refresh button. A method call is not awaitable and can do nothing before rendering; a real POS should make loading and action availability explicit. Your POS/backend remains responsible for prices, discounts and payment state. The SDK does not provide a payment-terminal or offline transaction API.
